note: Window agent p1830-p1839 (brief v2, run of 2 Nov 2026). Entries: events/0 West Prussia hole 1830-1833 (the 1815 keyframe leaves it out); events/1-4 Spanish leftover cells in Peru, Bolivia, Patagonia and Veracruz removed (the 1827 keyframe cut is below the snap threshold); keyframe_overrides/0 Egypt 1839 drawn without the Empty Quarter (the gazetteer Hasa is the whole Eastern Province); /1 New Mexico and west Colorado kept in the Mexican 1836 keyframe; /2 Buenos Aires frontier kept in 1834-1835; /3-5 the three US keyframes of the window get the Louisiana-overshoot cut that p1820-p1829 applied to its own

region.text: Prussia's provinces as Cliopatria draws them from 1834: West Prussia (Danzig, Pomerelia, Kulm land) and the rest that the 1815-1833 keyframe leaves unowned

events.note: Hole filled, 1830-1833: West Prussia is Prussian land throughout. The Province of Prussia page: 'was a province of the Kingdom of Prussia from 1829 to 1878'; 'An unpublished cabinet order of 3 December 1829 made the union official and created the Province of Prussia' (East and West Prussia, with Danzig the capital of West Prussia). The 1815-1833 keyframe (Cliopatria's German Confederation 1820 row) leaves about 130 cells of Pomerelia and Kuyavia unowned, which the 1834 keyframe snap (151 cells) then adds; this gain only moves the same land four years earlier. The hole began in 1815 (earlier windows).

region.text: the cells of Peru that Cliopatria's 1824 Spanish shape leaves to Spain (Titicaca shore, Ucayali), 37 cells

events.note: Leftover removed: Spain held no land on the South American mainland after 1826. Spanish American wars of independence page: 'The Spanish coastal fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé were the footholds that resisted until 1825-1826' and 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule'. The 1827 keyframe cuts the mainland (Peru, Bolivia, Argentina, Chile) but the cut is too small for a snap, so 47 cells stay Spanish in the draft.

region.text: the 2 Bolivian cells that the 1824 Spanish shape leaves to Spain

events.note: Leftover removed: the last royalists of Upper Peru surrendered after Olañeta died at Tumusla on 2 April 1825 (Spanish American wars of independence page); no Spanish land remained on the mainland after Callao and Chiloé (1825-1826).

region.text: the 8 Rio Negro cells (Carmen de Patagones coast) that the 1824 Spanish shape leaves to Spain

events.note: Leftover removed: the Spanish coastal footholds on the American mainland all fell by 1825-1826 (Spanish American wars of independence page: 'resisted until 1825–1826'; 'Only Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Spanish Virgin Islands and, briefly, Santo Domingo remained under Spanish rule'). Carmen de Patagones page: 'The town was founded in 1779 by Francisco de Viedma'; 'after the May Revolution of 1810, it became a prison for royalists'; 'The Brazilian troops attempted to take Carmen de Patagones, but they were repelled by armed residents on 7 March 1827' (the Cisplatine War). So the 8 cells go to the United Provinces (rio-de-la-plata, whose 1830 shape holds them and from which the Argentine Confederation takes them in 1831), not to nobody. Reviewer change (p1830-p1839 review, 2 Nov 2026): counterpart was 'nobody', which left the cells grey in 1830.

region.text: the 5 cells round San Juan de Ulúa that stay Spanish in the draft after the 1825 loss of the Veracruz fortress

events.note: Leftover removed: the Veracruz fortress is Spanish land only until 1825-1826. Spanish American wars of independence page: 'The Spanish coastal fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloé were the footholds that resisted until 1825–1826'. In the draft five coastal cells at 19 N, 96 W are still Spanish on 1 January 1830 (Spanish Empire /ledger/100 of 1825 did not take them) and are labelled 'Spanish Empire' on the 1830-1839 maps.

union.text: al-Hasa and Qatif as the Saudi state's 1830 shape holds them

minus.text: the Ha'il province, the Rashidi vassal emirate of the Saudi state

correction.text: the 1834 shape with Crete, the Tihama coast, Najd and the inhabited al-Hasa and Qatif (not the Empty Quarter), without the Ha'il province, after Faisal's defeat in 1838

keyframe_overrides.why: Expedition to Najd (1836) page: 'Mehmet Ali had occupied Najd, al-Hasa and Qatif' and 'in 1838 Mehmet Ali's forces commanded by Hurshid Pasha marched against Faisal and defeated him'. The dossier's correction takes the gazetteer's Hasa, which is the whole Eastern Province (2,447 cells to 17 N, the Rub' al-Khali): the draft gave Egypt 1,943 cells of empty desert and set it against the Trucial States (14 cells). Hasa is cut to the part the Nejd keyframe of 1830 holds (the oasis, Qatif and the coast), 490 cells.

union.text: New Mexico, a Mexican territory until 1846; Cliopatria's 1836 shape leaves out its west (251 cells)
Colorado and the strip of Wyoming south of 42N that lie west of 106 deg 20 min W, the meridian the Adams-Onis line follows north from the source of the Arkansas to 42N

correction.text: the northern Mexican lands under the Centralist regime, Alta California, all of New Mexico and the Colorado and Wyoming land west of 106 deg 20 min W

keyframe_overrides.why: Santa Fe de Nuevo México page: 'Under the 1824 Constitution of Mexico, it became the federally administered Territory of New Mexico'; 'the New Mexico Territory had been annexed under U.S. military occupation in September 1846'; the Texan claim to its east 'was disputed by Mexico' (the Santa Fe Expedition of 1841 was captured by New Mexican troops). Mexico held all 1,084 cells of New Mexico to the end of 1835; the 1836 keyframe snap turns 251 of them (the west) into unowned land through 1839. The Colorado and Wyoming land west of 106 deg 20 min W (about 330 cells), which Mexico holds from 1821 by data/patches/p1820-p1829.json events/0 (Adams-Onis line; that agent's page, not re-opened in this run), is also left out of Cliopatria's 1836 shape and would turn unowned: added to the keyframe.

correction.text: the 1834 shape with the Buenos Aires frontier of Rosas's 1833 expedition, without the Argentine Chaco

keyframe_overrides.why: Conquest of the Desert page: 'In 1833, Juan Manuel de Rosas in Buenos Aires Province ... coordinated offensives', 'only Rosas's expedition achieved some success' (it names no line). The dossier's own gain of 1833 (/ledger/1, confidence 2) gives the Confederation this land, and the 1836 shape holds it; the 1834-1835 shape lacks it, so the draft takes 107 Buenos Aires cells away in 1834 and returns them in 1836. Kept for 1834-1835 on the dossier's attribution to the 1833 expedition; the page names no boundary.

minus.text: the 1821 extent without the colony in Africa; the disputed north of Maine (Aroostook and the upper Saint John valley) is left out until the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842

the parts of Colorado, Oklahoma, Kansas and Wyoming south of the Arkansas River and west of its source that stayed Spanish under the Adams-Onis Treaty, Mexican from 1821 and ceded in 1848 (drawn as Cliopatria's Mexico shape of 1846 within the four states)

the 1821 extent without the colony in Africa; the disputed north of Maine (Aroostook and the upper Saint John valley) is left out until the Webster-Ashburton Treaty of 1842 Less the Spanish and later Mexican side of the Adams-Onis line (parts of Colorado, Oklahoma, Kansas and Wyoming), which the 'Louisiana' region overshoots.

union.text: Montana west of the Continental Divide (Flathead, Clark Fork and Bitterroot basins; the divide by Marias, Rogers, MacDonald and Homestake passes, the Anaconda Range and Chief Joseph Pass)
Wyoming west of the Continental Divide and north of 42N (the Snake and upper Green basins, west of the Wind River crest and South Pass)

the parts of Montana and Wyoming inside the Oregon Country, west of the Continental Divide and north of 42N, which the 'Louisiana' region of the US ledger overshoots into (the gazetteer's Oregon Country region is not used: in Montana it runs to 112W and takes in the Missouri-basin land east of the Divide)
Colorado and the strip of Wyoming south of 42N that lie west of 106 deg 20 min W, the meridian the Adams-Onis line follows north from the source of the Arkansas to 42N

minus.text: the Oregon Country part of Montana and the Spanish side of the Adams-Onis line in Colorado and Wyoming

correction.text: the keyframe's own correction less the Oregon Country parts of Montana and Wyoming (west of the Continental Divide) and the Colorado and Wyoming land west of the Adams-Onis meridian, Spanish then Mexican

keyframe_overrides.why: Same cut as data/patches/p1820-p1829.json keyframe_overrides/0-4, carried to the keyframes that start in this window (1830-1833). Oregon Country page (opened in this run): 'The two countries agreed to "joint occupancy" of the land west of the Rockies to the Pacific Ocean' (1818 convention) until 'the 1846 Oregon Treaty', and the region ran 'east to the Continental Divide ... as well as parts of Montana and Wyoming', so the Montana and Wyoming land west of the Divide was not exclusively US land; the dossier's 'Louisiana' region overshoots into it. The cut of the Colorado and Wyoming land west of 106 deg 20 min W, which the Adams-Onis line left to Spain and then Mexico, rests on the Adams-Onis Treaty page as quoted by the p1820-p1829 agent (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams%E2%80%93On%C3%ADs_Treaty); it was not re-opened in this run. Without the cut, the 1830 keyframe snap adds 732 cells to the US (330 taken from Mexico).
